```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# Keep this page synchronized with the current exported API. Deprecated
# compatibility markers are intentionally excluded from the reader path.
documented_exports <- c(
  "animal", "associate_pairs", "association", "beta", "beta_binomial", "bf",
  "biv_associate", "biv_gaussian", "biv_lognormal", "biv_student",
  "categorical", "centile_chart", "check_drm", "corpair", "corpairs",
  "cumulative_logit", "drm_control", "drm_formula", "drm_phylo_penalty",
  "drm_phylo_penalty_sweep", "drmTMB", "exceedance",
  "fitted_distribution", "fixef", "impute_model", "imputed",
  "is_converged", "latent_normal", "lognormal", "make_mesh",
  "marginal_parameters", "meta_V", "meta_vcov_bivariate", "mi",
  "miss_control", "nbinom2", "phylo", "phylo_interaction", "plot_corpairs",
  "plot_parameter_surface", "predict_parameters", "prediction_grid",
  "profile_targets", "qq_plot", "ranef", "relmat", "rho12", "rho_latent",
  "skew_normal", "spatial", "spatial_coords", "structured_effects", "student",
  "truncated_nbinom2", "tweedie", "worm_plot", "zero_one_beta"
)
deprecated_exports <- c("gr", "meta_known_V")
stopifnot(setequal(
  documented_exports,
  setdiff(getNamespaceExports("drmTMB"), deprecated_exports)
))
```

Use this page when you know what you want to do but not which function to
reach for. The map shows the usual path from model specification to plots; the
tables below cover every current exported function and the standard fitted-model
methods that users call directly.

This is a navigation guide, not a capability claim. A function can serve several
families or model structures while support remains narrower for a particular
combination. Check [What drmTMB can and can't do](capability-and-limits.html)
before treating an interval or a complex random-effect route as validated.
Deprecated compatibility markers are deliberately omitted.

## Model specification

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`drm_formula()` / `bf()`](../reference/drm_formula.html) | Combine one formula per distributional parameter. `bf()` is the short alias. |
| [`drmTMB()`](../reference/drmTMB.html) | Fit a univariate or bivariate distributional model. The native TMB engine is the default. |
| [`drm_control()`](../reference/drm_control.html) | Set optimizer controls and fitted-object storage or large-data options. |
| [`objective_at()`](../reference/objective_at.html) | Evaluate a fitted model's objective at a supplied parameter point, without refitting -- pairs with `drm_control(start = ...)` to compare a fit against another engine's answer. |
| [`meta_V()`](../reference/meta_V.html) | Supply known sampling variance or covariance for Gaussian meta-analytic models. |
| [`meta_vcov_bivariate()`](../reference/meta_vcov_bivariate.html) | Assemble the row-paired known covariance matrix for two-response meta-analysis. |
| [`miss_control()`](../reference/miss_control.html) | Choose the documented missing-response or missing-predictor policy. |
| [`mi()`](../reference/mi.html) | Mark a predictor whose missing values are modelled jointly with the response. |
| [`impute_model()`](../reference/impute_model.html) | Specify the family and formula for a modelled missing predictor. |

### Formula anatomy

| Syntax | What it controls |
|---|---|
| [`drm_formula(mu = trait ~ temp, sigma = ~ temp)`](../reference/drm_formula.html) | Model the expected trait and its residual scale with separate linear predictors. |
| [`nu = ~ 1`, `zi = ~ habitat`, `hu = ~ habitat`](../reference/drm_formula.html) | Add a shape, zero-inflation, or hurdle component where the chosen family supports it. |
| [`rho12 = ~ environment`](../reference/drm_formula.html) | Model coscale: the within-observation residual correlation of a bivariate Gaussian fit. |
| [`sd(group) ~ x`, `sd1(group) ~ x`, `sd2(group) ~ x`](../reference/random_effect_scale_formulas.html) | Model Gaussian location random-effect SDs; use `level = "phylogenetic"` for the documented structured route. |
| [`corpair(label) ~ x`](../reference/corpair.html) | Formula-marker syntax for a current q=2 labelled ordinary or phylogenetic location-location correlation block; predictors must be constant within group. |

### Response and predictor families

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`student()`](../reference/student.html) | Student-t location-scale-shape models for heavy-tailed continuous responses. |
| [`skew_normal()`](../reference/skew_normal.html) | Skew-normal location-scale-shape models. |
| [`lognormal()`](../reference/lognormal.html) | Positive continuous responses on the lognormal scale. |
| [`tweedie()`](../reference/tweedie.html) | Non-negative semicontinuous responses that may include exact zeroes. |
| [`beta()`](../reference/beta.html) | Strict proportions inside `(0, 1)`. |
| [`zero_one_beta()`](../reference/zero_one_beta.html) | Continuous proportions with structural exact zeroes or ones. |
| [`beta_binomial()`](../reference/beta_binomial.html) | Success counts with a known denominator and extra-binomial variation. |
| [`categorical()`](../reference/categorical.html) | An unordered categorical missing-predictor model in `impute_model()`. |
| [`cumulative_logit()`](../reference/cumulative_logit.html) | Ordered categorical responses or ordered missing-predictor models. |
| [`nbinom2()`](../reference/nbinom2.html) | Negative-binomial count models with quadratic mean-variance scaling. |
| [`truncated_nbinom2()`](../reference/truncated_nbinom2.html) | Positive or hurdle negative-binomial count models. |
| [`biv_gaussian()`](../reference/biv_gaussian.html) | Two Gaussian responses with separate means, scales, and residual `rho12`. |
| [`biv_lognormal()`](../reference/biv_lognormal.html) | Two lognormal responses with residual `rho12` on the log-response scale. |
| [`biv_student()`](../reference/biv_student.html) | Two heavy-tailed Student-t responses with a shared degrees-of-freedom parameter. |
| [`gaussian()`, `Gamma()`, `binomial()`, `poisson()`](distribution-families.html) | Base-R families for documented Gaussian, positive, event-count, and count-response routes. |

The package also accepts the base-R family constructors `gaussian()`,
`Gamma(link = "log")`, `binomial(link = "logit")`, and
`poisson(link = "log")` where documented. Zero-inflated and hurdle components
are selected through `zi = ~ ...` and `hu = ~ ...` formulas rather than separate
family constructors.

## Random and structured effects

| Function or syntax | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`animal()`](../reference/animal.html) | Pedigree or supplied animal-model precision/covariance structure. |
| [`phylo()`](../reference/phylo.html) | A structured effect derived from one phylogenetic tree. |
| [`phylo_interaction()`](../reference/phylo_interaction.html) | A pair-level effect derived from two phylogenetic trees. |
| [`spatial()`](../reference/spatial.html) | Coordinate-based spatial structured effects. |
| [`spatial_coords()`](../reference/spatial_coords.html) | Convert longitude and latitude to an explicitly chosen projected coordinate system. |
| [`make_mesh()`](../reference/make_mesh.html) | Build the fixed-kappa SPDE mesh and projection inputs used by mesh spatial effects. |
| [`relmat()`](../reference/relmat.html) | A structured effect from a user-supplied relationship or precision matrix. |
| [`corpair()`](../reference/corpair.html) | Mark one current q=2 labelled ordinary or phylogenetic location-location correlation formula. Keep this distinct from residual `rho12 = ~ ...`. |
| [`sd(group) ~ ...`, `sd1(group) ~ ...`, `sd2(group) ~ ...`](../reference/random_effect_scale_formulas.html) | Formula-only syntax for Gaussian location random-effect SDs. These are not replacements for `stats::sd()`. |
| [`drm_phylo_penalty()`](../reference/drm_phylo_penalty.html) | Define the documented penalized/MAP prior for weakly identified phylogenetic SDs or correlations. Penalized fits are MAP fits, not ordinary ML fits for LR tests or AIC comparisons. |
| [`drm_phylo_penalty_sweep()`](../reference/drm_phylo_penalty_sweep.html) | Check whether a penalized phylogenetic coupling is data-informed or prior-shaped. |

## Paired-outcome association

These functions create or inspect a separate `drm_pair_association` object.
They are not ordinary `drmTMB` fit extractors, and latent-normal association
`eta` is distinct from residual `rho12` and labelled random-effect
correlations returned by `corpairs()`.

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`biv_associate()`](../reference/biv_associate.html) | Fit two margins for a pair class listed in the association guide, then construct their frozen-margin association. |
| [`associate_pairs()`](../reference/associate_pairs.html) | Estimate within-row association from two fitted, aligned margins on a route listed in the association guide. |
| [`latent_normal()`](../reference/latent_normal.html) | Declare the Gaussian-copula kernel used by the paired-outcome association stage. |
| [`association()`](../reference/association.html) | Extract latent-normal `eta` from a separate `drm_pair_association` object. It is not residual `rho12` or a correlation from `corpairs()`. |

## Check, summarize, and extract

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`check_drm()`](../reference/check_drm.html) | Run the model-aware convergence and identifiability checks. Start here after fitting. |
| [`is_converged()`](../reference/is_converged.html) | Return one logical convergence summary for programmatic workflows. |
| [`summary()`](../reference/summary.drmTMB.html) | Print coefficients, fit information, and optional intervals. |
| [`coef()` / `fixef()`](../reference/fixef.html) | Extract fixed-effect coefficient blocks; `fixef()` makes the mixed-model meaning explicit. |
| [`ranef()`](../reference/ranef.html) | Extract conditional modes for ordinary or structured random effects. |
| [`sigma()`](../reference/sigma.drmTMB.html) | Extract fitted residual or family-specific scale values. |
| [`rho12()`](../reference/rho12.html) | Extract within-observation residual correlation for bivariate Gaussian fits. |
| [`corpairs()`](../reference/corpairs.html) | Extract labelled ordinary or structured latent-correlation summaries. |
| [`structured_effects()`](../reference/structured_effects.html) | List fitted structured-effect terms and their model roles. |
| [`imputed()`](../reference/imputed.html) | Summarize fitted values for a modelled missing predictor. |
| [`fitted()`](../reference/fitted.drmTMB.html) | Extract fitted response means for the original fitted rows. |
| [`residuals()`](../reference/residuals.drmTMB.html) | Compute the documented response, Pearson, or randomized-quantile residuals. |
| [`weights()`](../reference/weights.drmTMB.html) | Recover fitted likelihood weights. |
| [`logLik()`](../reference/model-fit-extractors.html) | Extract the unpenalized fitted log likelihood. |
| [`AIC()` / `BIC()`](../reference/model-fit-extractors.html) | Compare appropriate maximum-likelihood fits using information criteria. |
| [`vcov()`](../reference/model-fit-extractors.html) | Extract the fixed-effect covariance matrix when the Hessian is usable. |
| [`nobs()` / `df.residual()` / `deviance()`](../reference/model-fit-extractors.html) | Extract fitted-row count, residual degrees of freedom, or absolute negative twice log likelihood. |

## Intervals and likelihood profiles

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`profile_targets()`](../reference/profile_targets.html) | Discover direct fitted targets and their profile names before requesting an interval. |
| [`confint()`](../reference/confint.drmTMB.html) | Compute available Wald, profile-likelihood, or parametric-bootstrap intervals. |
| [`profile()`](../reference/profile.drmTMB.html) | Compute likelihood-ratio profiles for explicit targets. |
| [`plot()` for a profile](../reference/plot.profile.drmTMB.html) | Plot the likelihood-ratio curve, cutoff, estimate, and interval endpoints. |

Profile and bootstrap support is target-specific. Use `profile_targets(fit)` and
read the returned status instead of assuming that every printed parameter has a
calibrated interval.

## Prediction, simulation, and plots

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`prediction_grid()`](../reference/prediction_grid.html) | Build a new-data grid that varies selected predictors while controlling the others. |
| [`predict()`](../reference/predict.drmTMB.html) | Predict the response or a named distributional parameter for original or new data. |
| [`predict_parameters()`](../reference/predict_parameters.html) | Return several fitted distributional parameters in one tidy long table. |
| [`marginal_parameters()`](../reference/marginal_parameters.html) | Compute unweighted plug-in averages of fitted parameters on their moment-appropriate reporting scales; this is not an interval or contrast. |
| [`simulate()`](../reference/simulate.drmTMB.html) | Simulate new responses from a fitted model. |
| [`plot_corpairs()`](../reference/plot_corpairs.html) | Plot a table returned by `corpairs()`. |
| [`plot_parameter_surface()`](../reference/plot_parameter_surface.html) | Plot a table returned by `predict_parameters()` or a compatible parameter-surface table. |

## Distributional assessment

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`fitted_distribution()`](../reference/fitted_distribution.html) | Access fitted per-row density, CDF, and quantile functions. |
| [`exceedance()`](../reference/exceedance.html) | Compute conditional probability above or below a threshold. |
| [`centile_chart()`](../reference/centile_chart.html) | Plot conditional response centiles over one covariate. |
| [`qq_plot()`](../reference/qq_plot.html) | Plot randomized quantile residuals against normal quantiles. |
| [`worm_plot()`](../reference/worm_plot.html) | Detrend the QQ plot to reveal systematic departures. |

### Quick ecological recipes

| Task and code | Read it as |
|---|---|
| [`drmTMB(drm_formula(trait ~ temp, sigma = ~ temp), family = gaussian(), data = dat)`](../reference/drmTMB.html) | Ask whether both the expected trait and residual variability change with temperature. |
| [`drmTMB(count ~ habitat, family = nbinom2(), data = dat)`](../reference/nbinom2.html) | Model overdispersed abundance counts across habitats. |
| [`drmTMB(cbind(success, failure) ~ treatment, family = beta_binomial(), data = dat)`](../reference/beta_binomial.html) | Model success probability with extra-binomial variation. |
| [`check_drm(fit); predict(fit, newdata = grid)`](../reference/check_drm.html) | Check the fitted object before interpreting predictions on a controlled grid. |
| [`profile_targets(fit); confint(fit, method = "profile", parm = target)`](../reference/profile_targets.html) | Discover a direct target before requesting a profile-likelihood interval. |

### Interpretation guardrails

| Item | Remember |
|---|---|
| [`student()` scale](../reference/student.html) | Student-t `sigma` is a scale parameter, not the response standard deviation. |
| [`drm_phylo_penalty()` fits](../reference/drm_phylo_penalty.html) | These are penalized/MAP fits; `logLik()` reports the unpenalized data likelihood, and ordinary LR/AIC comparisons are not standard. |
| [Capability matrix](capability-and-limits.html) | A visible function does not imply every family-by-structure interval route is validated. |

## Optional Julia engine

Julia fitting is future/deferred work, not an optional route for a new
analysis. Current Julia methods provide compatibility for legacy Julia-engine
objects only.

| Function | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`rho_latent()`](../reference/rho_latent.html) | Extract the latent/link-scale correlation from a compatible legacy Julia-engine object. Julia fitting is not a current route for a new analysis. |

## What is intentionally absent

This cheatsheet excludes deprecated compatibility markers and their historical
spellings. Existing old scripts can still consult the full
[reference index](../reference/index.html), but new analyses should use
`meta_V()` rather than `meta_known_V()`, structured-effect markers rather than
`gr()`, and `sd(..., level = "phylogenetic")` rather than the legacy
`sd_phylo*()` spellings.
